steps.what: Attend hospital in-service programmes related to work specialization

tasks.design: Retain attendance, learning and practical questions during hospital training. Existing {LMS} materials may support the programme, but attendance is not an administrative step that vanishes when materials are digital.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safe specialised practice requires learning and clarification.
tasks.enabler_now: No new capability is assumed to shorten required learning.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding how procedures apply to actual equipment and exceptions.
tasks.human_edge: Ask practical questions and connect learning to safe work.
tasks.altitude: Learning time and training requirements remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Clarify shared preparation and handover requirements

evidence.claim: Training attendance remains learner effort; clinical documentation products do not establish a reduction in required learning time.

assumptions: Boundary is preparer training attendance, excluding trainer preparation and course administration.
Training provider produces the programme under existing processes; no automated competence flag or new structured input is assumed.
Use native training access first. Unchanged attendance adds no incremental upkeep.
research_questions: Which practical questions must be resolved before the procedure is applied?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Attendance, learning and questions retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Report defective equipment to responsible staff

steps.what: Confirm equipment identity and factual details of the defect report
Report defective equipment to the appropriate supervisor or technical staff

tasks.design: Configure a {HELPDESK} equipment form to assemble the report and suggest a responsible queue from a maintained directory. The preparer checks the exact message and recipient, confirms handover and uses immediate direct escalation for urgent safety concerns.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reporting repeats equipment details and requires finding the appropriate contact.
tasks.enabler_now: Native service forms and explicit asset-to-queue mappings can reduce repeated routing work.
tasks.still_hard: Unclear equipment ownership and urgent defects needing direct communication.
tasks.human_edge: Describe observed facts clearly and ensure the concern reaches a responsible person.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated report assembly, with unchanged safety judgement and handover responsibility.

reach.learn: Keep defect reports aligned with actual equipment status

evidence.claim: Native equipment defect forms and explicit queue mappings are plausible model knowledge; the digest has no equipment-reporting case or measured saving.

assumptions: Boundary is preparer defect reporting after detection, excluding equipment checks, repair and clinical decisions about alternative equipment. Existing safety procedures remain immediate and unchanged.

Preparer produces asset reference, location, observed symptom, observation time, urgency judgement and known isolation/status information in s1. Its full 40 hours include capture, identity checks and clarification; no structured defect code is assumed to exist beforehand.
Technical service owner maintains the asset-to-queue directory. Test native helpdesk forms first; unknown ownership or urgency requires direct human contact rather than guessed routing.
Four additional focal hours cover reporting exceptions and form checks; two technical-service hours cover directory and mapping corrections.
research_questions: Does form-based reporting reduce total effort after capture, recipient checks and handover acknowledgement?

already_counted.description: Report review, recipient confirmation and handover

incremental.description: Technical responsibility directory and mapping upkeep

approvals.approved_version: Exact asset, location, symptom, time, urgency/status account and recipient; changes require renewed send approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+48=88, gross=12, upkeep=4, net=8. High assumes 20% less report-stage assembly and contact lookup; low retains direct phone reporting for urgent or unmapped defects plus upkeep. Detection, safety checks and acknowledgement retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Start equipment using prescribed operating procedures
Observe gauges and equipment operation for malfunctions and prescribed-standard conformance

tasks.design: Retain physical startup and observation of equipment against prescribed standards. Existing {DOCS} operating procedures support checks; existing gauges and alarms are not newly removed human labour.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual operation must be checked for abnormal conditions beyond a nominal ready indicator.
tasks.enabler_now: No relevant validated inspection replacement is supplied in the digest.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising unusual sounds, readings or operating behaviour.
tasks.human_edge: Assess actual condition and stop unsafe operation within the authorised procedure.
tasks.altitude: Startup and operational checking time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Confirm prepared equipment is ready for use

evidence.claim: Physical startup and operational observation retain their time; automatic gauges do not themselves establish a labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary is preparer startup and operating-condition checks, excluding repair and separate defect reporting. Observation reused in a defect report is not counted twice.
Preparer produces the operating assessment in s2 with full observation time retained. No structured malfunction feed or automatic safe-to-use decision is assumed.
Use native operating procedures and alarms first. No changed system introduces upkeep.
unknowns: Existing alarms and required manual checks
research_questions: Which failure modes require direct observation despite existing gauges and alarms?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=30+70=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Startup and physical observation retain all time; existing gauge runtime earns no new labour saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: A small defect-report assembly gain is possible; specialised learning, equipment startup and operational checks remain hands-on work.
reach: Coordinate equipment readiness and unavailability with medical assistants
skills_to_grow: Separating device runtime from human checking effort
role.ambitious_version: A medical equipment preparer with clearer routed defect reports who retains practical equipment checks and safe work knowledge.
